D-FJ-1.title: A plan with TWO OR MORE arcs parsed to zero arcs -- and the guidance told the caller to send the shape it had just sent
D-FJ-1.note: MECHANISM. _section_level descends past a lone top heading whenever the level below it holds >=2 siblings, which is how it tells a document TITLE ('# Dracula's Legacy' + 4 sections) from a lone real section. A story plan is written '# 1. Arc Overview' then one '## ' per arc. With ONE arc the level below holds 1 and the `len(children) < 2` guard stops the descent BY LUCK; with the ordinary THREE arcs it holds 3, so the rule descended, read '# 1. Arc Overview' as the document's title, and promoted each ARC to a top-level section. The kind matcher cannot place an arc's name, so all three landed in `unclassified` and the spec parsed ZERO arcs. Both '# 1. Arc Overview' documents in the corpus behind the original rule happened to hold a single arc, so the shape was never actually protected -- the docstring's own table records the case as 'L2 has 1 -> STAY'. WHY IT IS UNRECOVERABLE, not merely wrong: plan_propose_spec is honest -- it returned problem='no_arcs_parsed' and guidance saying 'do NOT tell the author the plan is ready ... source_markdown must open with the line "# 1. Arc Overview" ... then one "## " heading per ARC, and under each arc one "### " heading per beat'. The model had ALREADY sent exactly that. An instruction the caller cannot satisfy is a loop, and the turn ended with the author told a chapter plan was 'ready to see and adjust' over a book with 0 structure_node, 0 outline_node and 0 chapters. FIX. In _section_level, stop descending when the lone heading at the current level is one the author NUMBERED (`_NUMBERED_SECTION = ^#{1,6}\s+\d+[.)]\s`). This is the parent-level twin of the `_DOTTED_SUB` rule already trusted one level down: `N.M` is the author saying 'this is part of section N', a bare `N.` is the author saying 'this IS section N'. It is the AUTHOR's signal, not the vocabulary's -- descending on 'is this heading a known kind?' was tried first by the original author and misread '# Story Premise: ...' as a section because 'premise' is vocabulary. The space after the dot is required, so '# 1.1 Ho So' remains a dotted sub-heading. All five unnumbered corpus titles descend exactly as before. CODE. Falsifier test_a_numbered_section_with_SEVERAL_arcs_is_still_not_a_title proven RED on the ORIGINAL defect, failing with the live symptom verbatim ('3 section(s) were read but matched no known kind: The Forged Path, The Salted Truth, The Great Unmapping'), then GREEN. Full suite 3739 passed / 403 skipped; a clean-HEAD worktree control ran 3738 passed, i.e. exactly the one test added and no regression. (One parallel-scheduling flake seen once in test_pack_budget_language_parity::test_vietnamese_is_not_starved_by_an_over_counting_encoder -- passed in isolation, passed in the clean-HEAD control, passed on re-run; pre-existing order dependence, carried below, not caused by this change.) LIVE. A/B through the browser, same prose, same model, same journey, only the fix differing -- book 019ff482 (before): problem='no_arcs_parsed', arcs=[], empty_read=true, unclassified=[3 arcs], sections_read=3, plan_run='proposed', structure_node=0, outline_node=0. Book 019ff497 (after): problem=null, arcs=3 ['The Forged Path','The Salt's Secret','The Great Unmapping'], events=6, unclassified=[], sections_read=1, plan_run='compiled', structure_node=3, outline_node=6. DATA. The 6 outline nodes are the chapter plan the author was promised and are grounded in the submitted prose ('Iseul discovers the first discrepancy in a most critical map.', 'The truth threatens the survival of Ashmere.', ...). Deployed by content, not by 'Built': image rebuilt and containers force-recreated, then per-file md5 of all 242 *.py verified difflines=0 against source on both composition-service and composition-worker.

D-FJ-2.title: The refusal for a missing argument asserted it was NOT an id, when the missing argument was an id
D-FJ-2.note: MECHANISM. CP-5.4 split the missing-required-argument refusal into two arms keyed off the tool's DECLARED argument_supplier: 'context|plan' gets "NOT yours to invent ... establish that context first (e.g. list or open the book you mean, then call this with the id it returns)", and everything else gets "These carry the actual CONTENT (not ids the system already fills) ... Do not call it with only ids". There is a THIRD case folded into the second: the tool declares NO supplier. declared_supplier returns None, None is not in ('context','plan'), so an undeclared argument silently inherits the model-supplied sentence -- and that sentence asserts a FACT about the missing arguments that nothing computed. Only 12 of the 315 federated tools carry a contract, so undeclared is the COMMON path, not the exotic one. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12: world_map_create refused for ['world_id'] with "These carry the actual CONTENT (not ids the system already fills) ... Do not call it with only ids or empty arguments." The one missing argument IS an id. The model was told the thing it lacked was not the thing it lacked, and told not to do the thing it needed to do; it stopped calling tools and claimed the map existed. FIX. A third arm: when any missing argument has no declared supplier, assert nothing that cannot be known -- name the arguments, forbid guessing, give the id move FIRST (obtain it from the tool that LISTS or SEARCHES those records) and the content move second. Not a reword: the old sentence makes a false claim about this call's data; the new one makes no claim it cannot support, which is the standard the context|plan arm already met. The three arms moved into one helper so the undeclared case cannot silently re-inherit the model-supplied sentence, and the call site was rewired to it. CODE. 5 new guards + 1 rewritten, ALL SIX proven RED by the repo's own harness (scripts/agentruntime-falsification.py run over just these rows: PROVEN 6, FAILED 0, each reddening its own named test, no bystanders). The pre-existing CP-5.4 guard had a falsifier anchored on the inline snippet this refactor removed; it was re-anchored and rewritten from a source-grep to a BEHAVIOURAL assertion, because a grep for the old expression would have gone red on a pure refactor while staying green on a message that consulted nothing -- the wrong way round for a guard. Full chat-service suite serial: 2875 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. (Under -n auto 18 tests fail and the clean-HEAD control itself crashed with an xdist INTERNALERROR; the CP suites spawn subprocesses and are parallelism-sensitive. Serial is the trustworthy signal here.) DATA. Before/after on the SAME input, with 'before' being the refusal actually recorded in loreweave_chat from the live failure and 'after' produced by the DEPLOYED image (verified difflines=0 against source): the phrase 'not ids the system already fills' and the instruction 'Do not call it with only ids' are gone, replaced by 'obtain it from the tool that LISTS or SEARCHES those records'. 🔴 WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: the model did not re-make the identical mistake after the fix -- the passing draw-a-map run called world_list first and produced no refusal, and a retry in the original session made zero tool calls -- so RECOVERY FROM THE NEW MESSAGE WAS NOT OBSERVED LIVE. The refusal text is proven changed on the deployed image for the exact failing input; the model's response to it is not claimed.

D-FJ-3.title: kg_build refused 'That is the ONLY precondition' on the call it had just refused for a different precondition
D-FJ-3.note: MECHANISM. target=graph has TWO gates: llm_model, checked in _handle_kg_build, and the project's embedding model, checked in _handle_kg_build_graph. They were enforced one per round trip, and the second one's message ended 'That is the ONLY precondition'. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12 (book 019ff497, project 019ff497-e068-77db-89f7-9d8c298fe8cd): call 1 kg_build{target:graph,project_id} -> refused, needs llm_model. Call 2 added llm_model='gpt-4o' -> refused for the embedding model WITH the exclusivity claim, i.e. a sentence denying the gate the same call had just failed. Call 3 repeated call 2 verbatim. The model then told the author 'I've started building the connection map' over a build that never started. The clause was only ever meant to say that kg_run_benchmark is advisory. FIX. Say exactly that and claim no exclusivity ('kg_run_benchmark ... does NOT gate this build'), and report EVERY unmet precondition of the requested target in ONE refusal rather than one per round trip. The project read happens only on the failure path, and errors it raises are the same ones the graph handler would raise a moment later, so they propagate rather than being swallowed into a second incomplete answer. CODE. Three guards, each proven RED by injecting the ORIGINAL code: restoring the exclusivity sentence reds test_a_refusal_never_claims_to_be_the_ONLY_precondition and nothing else; restoring the single-gate raise reds both test_BOTH_unmet_preconditions_are_named_in_ONE_refusal and test_a_SATISFIED_precondition_is_not_reported_as_unmet. The third guard is the control: with the embedding model configured the refusal names ONLY llm_model and says '1 precondition(s)', so listing a satisfied gate would be the same dishonesty pointed the other way. Full knowledge-service suite serial: 4204 passed, 3 failed -- all three reproduce IDENTICALLY on a clean-HEAD worktree control (test_kg_triage_list_default_is_bounded_and_summary, test_build_timeline_orders_and_maps, test_response_shapes_match_committed_snapshot), so they are pre-existing. (Under -n auto the run died with execnet MemoryError spawning workers -- a host resource limit, not a code failure; serial is the trustworthy signal.) DATA. Deployed by content: knowledge-service rebuilt and force-recreated, per-file md5 over all 301 *.py difflines=0 against source, and the deployed build_tools.py carries the new wording. THE JOURNEY IS STILL NOT COMPLETABLE, for a DIFFERENT defect recorded as D-FJ-4.

D-FJ-4.title: A refusal named the tools that unblock it, and none of them were on the model's surface
D-FJ-4.note: MECHANISM. kg_build's refusal says 'call kg_project_set_embedding_model first (pick one of your embedding models with settings_list_models)'. Both are federated -- present in the gateway's tools/list -- but MEASURED 2026-08-12 (session 019ff498-7603…) the turn's advertised surface carried kg_build and NEITHER of them; they were reachable only by discovering them through tool_list/tool_load. The model understood the requirement, wrote 'I'll get to work on setting that up now' three times, never called either tool, retried kg_build unchanged, and ended by asking the author whether to keep trying. An instruction naming an unreachable tool cannot be followed. FIX. Arm the catalogue tools a REFUSAL names, exactly as the dispatch chokepoint already does for an off-surface tool the model DID call ('making it round-trip through tool_list/tool_load to be told yes, that one is ceremony a weak model fails') and as D-NARRATED-WRITE does for a tool the model merely NAMED. A tool the RUNTIME named, in the sentence explaining how to proceed, was the strongest of the three cases and the only one uncovered. Whole-word matching, capped at 3, never re-arming what is already on-surface. CODE. 4 guards, all proven RED by the repo's harness (PROVEN 4, FAILED 0). One of them caught a real defect in ITS OWN first draft: the call-site guard grepped for '_tools_named_in_refusal(', which the function's own `def` line also contains, so it would have stayed green with the call site deleted — it now asserts the assignment. The harness also rejected the first falsifier for that guard as a BYSTANDER, because substituting an undefined name broke the import and a different test failed first. Full chat-service suite serial: 2879 passed, 0 failed. LIVE. The journey completed end to end through the browser on book 019ff542-1ad0-70c0-8c7d-b6066560d3aa, driven by google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat, no operator-typed tool argument. The log records `armed recovery tool(s) ['kg_project_set_embedding_model', 'kg_run_benchmark', 'settings_list_models'] named in kg_build's refusal`, and the model then CALLED settings_list_models and kg_project_set_embedding_model — the two tools it had previously only ever narrated. After the Tier-A approval the project gained embedding_model=019eeb08-8bff-75cb-8e86-700efd4033b5 and kg_build succeeded, minting its class-C confirm card. DATA. The decisive before/after is in the ARGUMENTS, not the prose: pre-fix the model invented llm_model='gpt-4o', a model this account does not own; post-fix the confirm token carries llm_model=019eeb08-8be3-78fb-86c0-3b1eda7e0457 and embedding_model=019eeb08-8bff-75cb-8e86-700efd4033b5, both real ids obtained from settings_list_models. Reaching the tool turned a hallucinated argument into a derived one.

D-FJ-5.title: A failure was emitted with NO message, so every layer reported an error nobody could act on
D-FJ-5.note: MECHANISM. On LM Studio's Responses stream, `response.failed`/`error` took ev.Message, fell back to ev.Response.Error.Message, and if BOTH were empty emitted the error frame anyway. StreamChunk.Message is `omitempty`, so the frame serialized to exactly {"event":"error","code":"LLM_UPSTREAM_ERROR"} — which is the string the SDK then raised, because loreweave_llm does raise from_code(ev.code, ev.message) and LLMError uses the default Exception __str__. The repo's own error_contract states 'message: required on every failure; a failure carrying no message is unrepresentable', and this path could emit precisely that. MEASURED: 3 chat turns across 3 books died this way on 2026-08-12 at 6% of a 200k context while a direct LM Studio probe answered normally; chat-service re-raised the bare code, provider-registry logged only its context preflight, worker-ai logged nothing. The loop could not tell a model crash from a bad payload from a transport fault. FIX. When both upstream sources are empty, say what IS known — the event type, the response id and the upstream status, all already on the frame and all three actionable (the id is greppable in the provider's own logs; the status separates `failed` from a bare `error`). It invents nothing; it reports fields the frame carried and discarded. CODE. Falsifier proven RED by injecting the original behaviour: the guard fails with 'a failure was emitted with NO message'. Its CONTROL — a real upstream message must never be overwritten — stayed green under the same injection, as did the pre-existing FailedSurfacesError test. Full provider-registry suite: all 6 packages ok. DATA. Deployed by content, not by 'Built': the binary in the running container contains the new string (grep over /proc/1/exe = 1).

D-FJ-6.title: One translatable block produced ZERO batches, and the failure blamed an LLM step that never ran
D-FJ-6.note: MECHANISM. `build_batch_plan` skips any entry whose text is empty ('if not text_to_translate: continue'), but `translatable_count` counted every entry whose ACTION was 'translate', empty or not. The count and the batcher disagreed about what 'translatable' means. A chapter of empty blocks then reported translatable_count=1 with 0 batches, and chapter_worker's total-failure guard ('translatable_count > 0 and translated_count == 0') fired over a stage that had never run. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12, job 019ff568-5b93-7a55-b26c-ebfec28be145 (book 019f8027, en→vi): BOTH chapters hold exactly ONE 'paragraph' block with text_content of length 0 (verified in chapter_blocks). The worker logged '1 blocks (1 translate, 0 pass, 0 caption) → 0 batches' and raised 'translation produced no output: 0/1 blocks translated (LLM step failed for every batch — see worker log)'. No LLM call was ever made; there was no batch to make one with. The job row was left status='failed' with error_message EMPTY, so the user's translation failed with the blame pointed at the wrong component. FIX. Count what the batcher will actually translate — action AND text. The guard itself is correct and STAYS: a chapter whose blocks do carry text and whose LLM step fails still has translatable_count > 0 and must still raise, because the pipeline falls each failed block back to its original text and persisting that as 'completed' is the silent false-success the guard was built to stop. Only the denominator changed, to the one the batcher uses. CODE. Two guards proven RED by restoring the original count; the CONTROL (a real block is still counted, so the guard stays armed) stayed green under the same injection — without it this fix could have silenced the guard instead of correcting it. Full translation-service suite serial: 1164 passed, 0 failed. DATA. Before/after on the DEPLOYED image (difflines=0 on both translation-service and translation-worker), against the exact failing input: empty chapter → translatable_count 1→0, batches 0, total-failure guard would fire FALSE (it fired TRUE before); real chapter → translatable_count=1, batches=1, guard still armed.

D-FJ-7.title: The model sent ['vi'] for a scalar enum and the turn ended on the refusal
D-FJ-7.note: MECHANISM. translation_start_job was called with target_language=['vi'] and refused: "Input should be 'en', 'vi', … (you sent ['vi'])". The refusal is exemplary — it names the legal set AND what was sent — and the turn still ended there. This is the typed-params class (16.8% of the recorded corpus), and a one-element list where a scalar is declared is its most mechanical shape: the value the model chose is already correct, only its container is wrong. FIX. Unwrap ['x'] → 'x' before the missing-argument check and before dispatch, ONLY where the schema says the param cannot be a list. 🔴 THE SHAPE THAT MATTERED WAS THE ONE THE FIRST DRAFT DECLINED: the real catalogue declares target_language as anyOf:[{enum,string},{null}] — pydantic's rendering of `X | None` — and the first version refused every anyOf, so the repair could not fire on the very call that motivated it. Measured against the LIVE gateway schema, not an invented one, then widened to flatten one union level while requiring every non-null branch to be scalar. CODE. 8 guards, ALL proven RED by the repo's harness (PROVEN 8, FAILED 0, no stale anchors). The harness earned its keep three times here: it called two of my controls 'GREEN — the guard requires nothing' because each was protected by a clause I had not targeted (the bare-array case is declined by the positive scalar requirement, not by the array clause), and it rejected a third falsifier as a BYSTANDER. Each control now needs BOTH type-guard clauses removed to red — which is the honest 'no protection' state. Full chat-service suite serial: 2887 passed, 0 failed. DATA. Deployed by content (difflines=0). The repair is deliberately conservative and did NOT fire in the follow-up live runs, because the model sent the scalar correctly — recorded as-is rather than dressed up: what is proven is that the repair fires on the exact recorded shape and refuses every list-capable schema, not that it rescued a live turn.

D-FJ-8.title: A write claimed in plain language, naming no tool, is invisible to the narrated-write guard
D-FJ-8.note: MECHANISM. The D-NARRATED-WRITE guard finds a claimed write by intersecting the model's prose with real tool NAMES and filtering to write tiers — deliberately mechanical, 'no NLP, no claim-parsing, no guessing at tense'. It therefore fires ONLY when the model names a tool. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12, book 019f9a02-f3a3…: asked 'Please translate this book into Vietnamese for me now', the model answered "I've started the translation for Chapter 1 into Vietnamese. I'll monitor the progress…" with ZERO tool calls, outcome='completed', and no job row. It named no tool, the intersection was empty, and NO D-NARRATED-WRITE line appears for that turn. The plainer phrasing — the one a user actually gets — was structurally invisible. FIX. A sister arm that also refuses to read the prose: fire when `attempted` is EMPTY (the turn called nothing, so nothing can have changed) AND a rail has a next actionable step whose tool is a WRITE tier (a concrete, journey-declared action was outstanding). It asserts NOTHING about what the model claimed, because a runtime that accuses the model of a claim it never measured is the same false-report defect pointed the other way — three of which this loop has already fixed. CODE. 6 guards, all proven RED by the repo's harness (PROVEN 6, FAILED 0, no stale anchors), including four that keep it from over-firing: a turn that ATTEMPTED a tool, a rail whose next step is a READ, no rail at all, and a completed rail with no next step. Full chat-service suite serial: 2893 passed, 0 failed. LIVE A/B, same prose, same book, only the fix differing — BEFORE: no D-NARRATED-WRITE line at all. AFTER: 'D-NARRATED-WRITE … nudging once'. The detection is proven. 🔴 TWO DEFECTS IN THIS FIX'S OWN FIRST DRAFT, both found by reading its live output rather than its tests: (1) the WARNING line was shared with the other arm, so it logged 'named in prose' about prose this arm never reads — the directive had been written carefully and the log had not; fixed and now guarded. (2) It returns the FIRST rail with an outstanding write, so on a translation request it nudged toward vision-to-book's `kg_add_nodes` rather than the rail matching the request — recorded as OBS-14, its own cycle, because selecting the rail that matches the user's intent needs the intent-pin flag threaded from stream_response into _emit_chat_turn. 🔴 AND THE RESIDUAL, STATED PLAINLY: after the nudge the model STILL ended with zero tool calls and still wrote 'I have already started the translation for Chapter 1'. What is proven is that the runtime now DETECTS and nudges the case it was blind to; it is NOT proven that the nudge changes this model's behaviour. That is why translation-pass stays blocked.

D-FJ-9.title: A bare verb STEM behind word boundaries missed the forms a user actually writes
D-FJ-9.note: MECHANISM. `intent_pinned_workflows` is a hand-maintained regex table matched against a HUMAN SENTENCE, and translation-pass's only verb pattern was ` translate ` — which matches neither 'translating' NOR 'translation', the two forms a user is most likely to write, for the rail literally named translation-pass. Same blindness at ` triage ` ('triaging'/'triaged'). MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12: 'Check what in this book still needs translating into Vietnamese, and bring the translation up to date' pinned NOTHING; the turn engaged a stale vision-to-book rail and no translation tool was called. REPRODUCED WITH NO MODEL IN THE LOOP — the function takes prose and returns slugs, so the live sentence is a unit-test row: it returned []. FIX. Enumerate the ordinary inflections at both sites (` translat(e|es|ed|ing|ion|ions) `, ` triag(e|es|ed|ing) `) rather than widening to a prefix — the CONTROL forbids `translat\w*`, which would pin on 'transatlantic'; 'triangle' and 'translator' must also stay unpinned. CODE. Falsifier proven RED by restoring the bare stems: the live-sentence guard, the all-forms guard and the triage guard all fail; the over-correction control stays green under the same injection. Full chat-service suite serial: 2897 passed, 0 failed. NOT registered in scripts/agentruntime_falsifiers.py — that harness enumerates the agentruntime CP suites only, and test_intent_workflows.py is outside them, so the row would have been reported 'no such guard in either suite'. Proven by direct injection instead, which is what the other services in this run use. LIVE A/B on the exact recorded sentence: BEFORE — nothing pinned, 'rail vision-to-book: 3/9' engaged. AFTER — 'intent pinned workflow(s) [translation-pass]', 'rail translation-pass: 2/3 steps done, next=translation_start_job', and translation_start_job actually ran. REMAINING AND SEPARATE: the other two recorded instances are a DIFFERENT sub-mechanism — competing/missing patterns rather than inflection. 'connect them so I can see how they relate' genuinely matches kg-build's `how.*they.*relate`, so that is a precedence question between two correct matches; and autonomous-drafting has no pattern for 'drafting itself chapter by chapter'. Recorded as OBS-15, its own cycle.

D-FJ-10.title: The workflow's own description did not pin the workflow
D-FJ-10.note: MECHANISM. autonomous-drafting's description reads 'drafting itself chapter by chapter, on its own', and not one of its four patterns (`draft.*next.*(chapter|few)`, `keep (writing|drafting)`, `write.*(several|multiple).*chapter`, `draft.*while i`) matched a user who wrote exactly that. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12, book 019ff497 — the only book carrying this workflow's stated precondition: 'Set this book drafting itself chapter by chapter from the plan, and pause for me to review before it goes too far' pinned NOTHING; the only rail computed was a completed vision-to-book (9/9), so none of the five declared steps was reached. Reproduced with no model in the loop. FIX. Add the three phrases that make it AUTONOMOUS rather than single-chapter — 'chapter by chapter', 'draft(ing) itself', 'on its own … draft/writ' — which is exactly the line against chapter-compose. CODE. Falsifier proven RED by removing the three patterns (the live-sentence guard and the phrase guard both fail); the CONTROL — 'Please write this chapter for me' must still pin chapter-compose and NOT autonomous-drafting — stays green under the same injection, which is what stops this widening from stealing the single-chapter case. Full chat-service suite serial: 2900 passed, 0 failed. LIVE A/B on the exact recorded sentence: BEFORE — nothing pinned, only 'rail vision-to-book: 9/9 steps done, next=—'. AFTER — 'intent pinned workflow(s) [autonomous-drafting]' and 'rail autonomous-drafting: 0/5 steps done, next=plan_bootstrap_propose'.

D-FJ-11.title: The model invented 'run_12345_placeholder' for a plan-supplied id, and the refusal only argued about its TYPE
D-FJ-11.note: MECHANISM. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12 (autonomous-drafting, book 019ff497): the model called plan_compile with run_id='run_12345_placeholder' and was refused 'run_id must be a UUID' — correct about the TYPE and silent about the thing that matters. run_id is a PLAN value emitted by plan_propose_spec; it is not the model's to invent, and arguing about its format only invites a better-formatted invention. This is CP-5.4's lesson ('you forgot something' vs 'I owe you this') one state to the right: the argument is PRESENT and fabricated, so the missing-arg path never ran and the honest sentence never fired. TWO SITES, ONE MECHANISM — the argument-supplier contract deciding the refusal — so by the RUNBOOK's test they had to be fixed in ONE cycle: (a) plan_compile.run_id and plan_bootstrap_apply.proposal_id are now DECLARED `plan` (the registry held 12 of 315 tools and neither of these), and (b) a `plan`-declared `*_id` present with a non-UUID value is dropped before dispatch and reported through the existing owed arm. Declaring without the check would have left the live failure untouched; checking without declaring would have had nothing to check. 🔴 THE SUITE CAUGHT A REAL OVER-FIRE IN THE FIRST DRAFT, which is why the scope is `plan` and not `context|plan`: including context deleted book_id='b1' — a value the RUNTIME injects upstream and which is not guaranteed to be a UUID — breaking the dispatch entirely (5 tests red). A context id is not the one the model invents; a plan id is. That is now its own control. CODE: 9 guards, all proven RED by the repo's harness (PROVEN 9, FAILED 0, no stale anchors) — and the harness again rejected two of my own falsifiers as 'GREEN — the guard requires nothing': replacing UUID(value) with `pass` makes the checker accept everything, and an ACCEPTANCE guard can only be reddened by making it REJECT; and the early `not contract` return also protected the undeclared case, so that row needed two edits. Full chat-service suite serial: 2909 passed, 0 failed. DATA: deployed by content (difflines=0) AND the registry verified present IN THE IMAGE with plan_compile among its 14 contracts — a registry absent from the image is a silently dead mechanism. LIVE A/B, same prose, same book: BEFORE "run_id must be a UUID — received 'run_12345_placeholder'"; AFTER "'plan_compile' is missing ['run_id'], and this is NOT yours to invent: the runtime supplies it from the current context or an active plan, and has none right now. Establish that context first … Do NOT guess a value."

D-FJ-12.title: The owed refusal knows which tool emits the missing id and does not say it
D-FJ-12.note: MECHANISM. After D-FJ-11 made the refusal honest, the model was correctly told run_id is 'NOT yours to invent … Establish that context first (e.g. list or open the book you mean…)' — and it retried plan_compile TWICE, because that sentence is GENERIC: a book-flavoured example that names no tool. The emitter was already written down in the contract's own identifier_resolution prose ('an opaque id emitted by plan_propose_spec') and the message threw it away — the same shape as D-FJ-3 (blocking rules computed and discarded) and D-FJ-5 (a failure emitted with its message removed). FIX. Declare the emitter as DATA and say it. Not parsed out of the explanation, because deciding behaviour from prose is precisely what declared_supplier refuses to do ('the explanation is for a human'). 🔴 THE MEMBRANE GATE REJECTED THE FIRST DRAFT and was right: `emitted_by` as a member of a contract row violates tool contract 1.0.0's closed member set, which the gate enforces on every read ('a released row must satisfy the tool contract every time the file is read'). Carrying one map is not a reason to bump a released contract version, so the emitters live in `argument_emitters`, a SIBLING of `contracts`. Gate green after the move. IT ALSO COMPOSES WITH D-FJ-4: naming the emitter ARMS it, because that arm keys off catalogue names found in the refusal text — one sentence fixes the instruction and the reachability together, and a guard asserts exactly that. CODE. 4 guards, all proven RED by the repo's harness, no stale anchors — including the CONTROL that the generic sentence SURVIVES where no emitter is declared, since most contracts declare none and inventing one would be a guess. Fixing an ambiguous anchor was part of this: '"plan_compile": {' now matches twice (the contract row and the emitters map), and a two-occurrence anchor is a stale row. Full chat-service suite serial: 2913 passed, 0 failed; membrane gate OK. DATA. Deployed by content (difflines=0) with argument_emitters verified present IN THE IMAGE. Before/after on the deployed image for the exact failing input: BEFORE '… Establish that context first (e.g. list or open the book you mean…)'; AFTER '… Call plan_propose_spec first, then call this with the id it returns.' The control on the same image still yields the generic sentence for book_read.book_id, which declares no emitter. 🔴 WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: the model did not call plan_compile again after the deploy — it had already concluded it was stuck — so the new sentence was not exercised by a live turn. It is proven changed on the deployed image for the exact input; the model's response to it is not claimed.

D-FJ-13.lives_in: composition tools' book/work id argument + chat-service's cross-book override (which covers book_id only)
D-FJ-13.title: A REAL id of the WRONG TYPE reached the tool, and the answer was the uniform not-accessible error
D-FJ-13.note: MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12 in a FRESH session on book 019ff497 (the stuck session was deleted first, which is what let the model reach the rail's real first step at all). With D-FJ-10 the rail engaged — 'rail autonomous-drafting: 0/5 steps done, next=plan_bootstrap_propose' — and the model called plan_bootstrap_propose, the correct first step, which suspended on its Tier-A gate. After approval it failed 'not found or not accessible', as did composition_package_tree and composition_diagnostics. NOT an outage: /health/federation reported composition available and composition-service healthy. The composition-service log names the cause — its last access check is GET /internal/books/019ff497-e068-77db-89f7-9d8c298fe8cd/access, and that uuid is the KNOWLEDGE PROJECT id for this book, not the book id (the book is 019ff497-dff3-7f26-9565-7e284f7ca71c). The model passed a REAL id of the WRONG TYPE, and the tool answered with the uniform ownership error, which by design says nothing about which id was wrong. Note chat-service ALREADY has the right instinct one field over: it logs 'tool arg book_id=… differs from the studio's book … — overriding (a cross-book target here is a hallucination)'. That override covers `book_id` and did not cover whatever argument carried the project id here. Two halves for its own cycle: find which parameter took it, and decide whether the studio's single-book override should extend to it — plus whether a uniform not-accessible answer should distinguish 'no such thing' from 'not yours' for an id the runtime could have checked the TYPE of.

carried_observations.note: FE agent-status reads 'Dang chay cong cu - <tool>' (running tool) while chat-service has already persisted outcome=awaiting_input for the turn. Observed at both gates, on the verified stack, in every run. Turn-outcome and call-outcome are two vocabularies; the chip is showing the last call and calling it the turn's state.

chat-service terminal-persist wrote the SAME assistant message id twice with conflicting outcomes: first outcome=crashed, then outcome=awaiting_input (session 019ff466-c571-7843-a67f-a0083b40b982, msg d6393215-c9c5-4ef5-b60c-f76d2012d06f, 0 chars both times). A gate-suspended turn appears to transit through 'crashed'.

Tier-A permission card renders three buttons localized ('Cho phep mot lan', 'Luon cho phep', 'Tu choi') and the fourth raw English ('Never allow') -- one missing key in one component. composition-service test_pack_budget_language_parity::test_vietnamese_is_not_starved_by_an_over_counting_encoder failed once under `-n auto --dist load` and passed in isolation, in a clean-HEAD control, and on re-run. Pre-existing order dependence, not caused by D-FJ-1.

Only 12 of 315 federated tools declare an `argument_supplier` contract, so CP-5.4's precise 'the runtime owes you this' arm can never fire for the other ~303 -- including every world_* tool, where world_id is a plan value emitted by world_list (the rail's own first step). D-FJ-2 makes the undeclared case honest rather than wrong; DECLARING these contracts is a separate cycle.

The `draw-a-map` rail has no world-create step, and 74 of this account's 76 active novels have world_id NULL. It is satisfiable only because the account already owns 28 worlds for world_list to return -- from a genuinely fresh account the declared journey has no first move. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE in the passing run: asked to draw 'a map of a world for this story', the model picked an unrelated pre-existing world named 'S10 World probe' and created the map there. The map, its Ashmere marker and its Ring of Salt Flats region are all real and correct, but the book they were drawn for still has world_id NULL, so nothing binds them to it. The four declared steps all completed, which is why the journey is proven; that the rail cannot bind a world to the book is a gap in the DECLARED journey, for its own cycle.

The `kg-build` rail is glossary_book_ontology_read -> kg_project_create -> kg_add_nodes -> kg_build, with no step that configures the project's embedding model -- yet kg_project_create creates the project with embedding_model NULL and kg_build hard-requires it. Same shape as OBS-9: the declared journey omits a step its own last step demands.

A long book-studio session died with LLM_UPSTREAM_ERROR and chat-service stamped 'CP-0.4 orphaned turn: no assistant row, outcome failed' on the user message. The session had accumulated 467,340 input tokens over 9 messages against a 195K-usable context. The UI's own context meter read 10%.

The intent pinner engaged the WRONG rail again, and this time it was not recoverable. For 'Check what in this book still needs translating into Vietnamese, and bring the translation up to date' — a near-paraphrase of translation-pass's own description — stream_service logged 'rail vision-to-book: 3/9 steps done, next=glossary_book_ontology_read'. translation-pass was never pinned. Same class as OBS-4 (kg-build pinned for a vision-to-book request), but there the correct rail still ran; here the model called composition_package_tree and no translation tool at all.

Turns die as LLM_UPSTREAM_ERROR / outcome='crashed' with 0 chars, and no layer records the upstream reason. Observed 3 times across 3 books on 2026-08-12 at 6% context use (provider-registry's own preflight: input_tokens=12,344 / context_length=200,000) while a direct LM Studio /v1/chat/completions probe answered normally — so it is neither context nor a dead model. NARROWED, and this is the lead worth starting from: the SDK raises `from_code(ev.code, ev.message)` and the resulting exception text is literally '{"event": "error", "code": "LLM_UPSTREAM_ERROR"}'. loreweave_llm's ErrorEvent.message is a REQUIRED pydantic field, so the frame did carry a message — and that message is OUR OWN error frame, serialized. provider-registry emits `Message: err.Error()`, so an error frame appears to be getting wrapped in itself on the hop: the inner frame becomes the outer frame's message, and the real upstream reason (whatever LM Studio actually said) is what got replaced. That is why every layer looks like it is 'logging the error' while the operator learns nothing. Suspect sites: stream_handler.go:492 (post-Stream emit) vs the adapter-level emits, and whatever returns an already-framed error up through adapter.Stream.

_rail_write_step_stalled returns the FIRST rail carrying an outstanding write step, not the rail matching the user's request. Measured 2026-08-12 on a translation ask: it nudged toward vision-to-book's kg_add_nodes (rail 8/9 done) while translation-pass was the pinned intent. The correct selector is the intent-pinned slug, which `stream_response` computes (`_intent_slugs`) but does not thread into `_emit_chat_turn`/`_stream_with_tools`. Own cycle.

Two intent-pin instances remain after D-FJ-9, and they are a different sub-mechanism from the inflection fix. (a) PRECEDENCE: 'Please set up this book's world categories, capture the cast … connect them so I can see how they relate, and give me a chapter plan' still pins ['kg-build'], because it genuinely matches kg-build's `how.*(they).*(relate)`. Both matches are defensible; there is no rule for which wins, and vision-to-book has no patterns of its own (it is mode-pinned by the binding, per the module's own docstring). (b) COVERAGE: autonomous-drafting's patterns (`draft.*next.*(chapter|few)`, `keep (writing|drafting)`, `write.*(several|multiple).*chapter`, `draft.*while i`) match none of 'Set this book drafting itself chapter by chapter from the plan', so that journey never started. Both are unit-testable with no model in the loop.

DQ-30.question: When the target model narrates a write instead of performing it, and the runtime's nudge does not change that, what is the product's answer? Options seen from here, none chosen: (a) the runtime executes the rail's next declared step itself once the nudge is ignored (the rail already names the tool and the step is gated, so consent is not bypassed); (b) the turn is reported to the AUTHOR as 'no action was taken' rather than ending on the model's claim; (c) the journey is declared out-of-reach for this model tier and the surface says so.
DQ-30.evidence: MEASURED 2026-08-12 with all eight fixes deployed and verified by content. Book 019f9cf7-0ae3-79e6-b93f-37b9ce9e573c, prose 'Please translate this book into Vietnamese for me now'. The runtime did everything it can currently do: the rail was computed with next=translation_start_job, D-FJ-8's arm fired correctly — 'the turn called NO tool while a rail's next write step is outstanding: [translation_start_job] — nudging once' — and the directive told the model to either call it or say plainly that it did not. The model still ended the turn with ZERO tool calls, outcome='completed', and no job row; on the sister book it wrote 'I have already started the translation for Chapter 1' after the same nudge. Every declared step of this workflow HAS been observed succeeding live in other runs, so the tools work; what does not work is getting this model to take the step when it has decided to narrate instead. That is a product decision about what the runtime owes the author when the model will not act, not a further defect to fix by measurement.
